# Quill

> Quill is a free, open-source Telegram client for macOS, Windows and Linux, written from scratch in Rust. It signs in to a normal Telegram account through Telegram's own TDLib library and draws its whole interface on the GPU with GPUI, the UI framework from the Zed editor. It is an independent project, not made by or affiliated with Telegram.

Key facts:

- Platforms: macOS 14 or later on Apple Silicon, Windows 10 or later on x64, Linux on x86_64 or arm64 with glibc.
- Price and license: free, MIT license. Source code: https://github.com/shinycake/quill
- Install: one command per system (Terminal on macOS, PowerShell on Windows, a terminal on Linux), or a zip/tarball from GitHub Releases. Each release publishes SHA-256 checksums.
- Memory: on an Apple M1 Pro Mac (macOS 27.0.1, 8 October 2026), Quill used about a third of the memory of Telegram Desktop 7.2.9 a minute after launch, and about 40% as much after opening five chats. Physical footprint from macOS `footprint`, median of three runs.
- Launch: on the same Mac (18 October 2026), Quill's window was on screen about four times faster than Telegram Desktop 7.3.1's on a warm launch, and about twice as fast on a cold launch. Windows and Linux have not been measured.
- HDR photos: photos sent as files are shown in high dynamic range. On macOS with an XDR or HDR screen: iPhone HEIC with a gain map, and AVIF or HEIC in PQ or HLG. On Windows with HDR on: Ultra HDR and gain-map JPEG, and HDR JPEG XL. Linux shows the standard-range picture.
- Features: formatted messages, replies, forwarding, scheduled and silent messages, cloud drafts, reactions, polls; photos, videos, albums, GIFs, stickers, voice and video messages with transcription; one-to-one audio and video calls with screen sharing and group voice chats; group and channel admin tools, forum topics, comments, statistics, bots; secret chats, passcode lock, active sessions, two-step verification; themes, accent colors, wallpapers and multiple accounts.
- Privacy: data stays on the computer, encrypted with a key in the macOS keychain, Windows DPAPI or a private file on Linux. No analytics in the app. Besides Telegram, the app only contacts GitHub to check for updates, which can be switched off.
- Status: early, experimental software with no warranty. Users should keep an official Telegram app installed.

## Agent access

- What it is: AI agents on the user's own computer (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor or any MCP client) use the user's Telegram account through the Quill that is already running.
- Off by default; while it is off, the only trace in Quill is one switch. The user turns it on in Quill: Settings > Advanced > Agent access.
- MCP: `quill mcp` is a stdio MCP server, a mode of the Quill executable. Claude Code: `claude mcp add quill -- <path to quill> mcp`. `quill agent connect claude-desktop|cursor --yes` merges the entry into that app's config after a backup.
- Command line: `quill agent <command>` reaches the same tools without MCP (`status`, `chats`, `read`, `send`, `search`, `call <tool> --json '{…}'`). `quill agent describe` prints every tool's schema, example and output as JSON; exit codes name each failure (3 Quill not running, 4 access off, 5 token, 6 window control off). On Windows the command line is `quill-cli.exe`, next to `quill.exe`; it waits and passes the exit code on.
- Skill: `quill agent install-skill` writes a Claude Code Agent Skill to `~/.claude/skills/quill`.
- What agents can do: read, search and send in the chats the user grants (by default Saved Messages, bots and the user's own channels), edit, react, pin, drafts, folders, raw TDLib calls under the same grants, and, with a second switch, click and type in Quill's window. Quill asks the user before anything outside the grants. Sends are paced and logged, and can wait for the user's click.
- Guardrails: Quill never sends data to any AI service itself. There is no network listener, only a local socket with a per-launch token. Read receipts, online status and typing are never suppressed. No bulk export. Telegram's terms do not allow training AI models on the data.
- [Agent guide](https://github.com/shinycake/quill/blob/main/src/agent/guide.md): tools, grants, recipes and errors.
- [Agents section](https://shinycake.github.io/quill/#agents)
